name: The three scopes (persons of small, middling and great capacity)

definitions.definition: Atiśa's division of practitioners by motivation: the lesser seeks saṃsāric happiness (higher rebirth), the middling seeks their own peace (liberation), the supreme seeks the end of all beings' suffering (buddhahood).
The lamrim's structure: the practices of the small and middling scopes are trained as 'common' preliminaries leading to the great scope, so that every teaching becomes a step to buddhahood.
Correlated by Sakya teachers with the first three lines of Parting from the Four Attachments.

relations.note: lines 1–3 of Parting correspond to the three scopes; line 4 to the view
renunciation ~ middling scope, bodhicitta ~ great scope

name: The three visions (snang gsum) of the Lamdre

definitions.definition: Impure vision: appearances of beings under the afflictions; experiential vision: appearances to the yogin in concentration; pure vision: the Sugatas' inexhaustible ornamental wheel of body, speech and mind. The common Lamdre path is taught through them.

members: impure vision (ma dag pa'i snang ba)

relations.note: impure vision covers the small and middling scope topics, experiential vision the bodhicitta of the great scope

name: The three continua (rgyud gsum) of the Lamdre

definitions.definition: The causal continuum (the all-base, clarity-emptiness, containing saṃsāra and nirvāṇa), the method continuum (the body and the practices of empowerment and the two stages — the 'explanatory continuum') and the result continuum (Mahāmudrā).

members: all-base causal continuum (kun gzhi rgyu rgyud)
Mahāmudrā result continuum (phyag rgya chen po 'bras bu'i rgyud)

name: Signs of the grounds in the Vajra Verses

definitions.definition: The Vajra Verses mark each ground by an inner sign (the stopping of a measure of wind, in finger-widths) and an outer sign (the drop stabilised at a place of the body), together with powers such as shaking and visiting emanation fields.

name: The thirteen grounds and Vajradhara

definitions.definition: The tantric path of the Lamdre culminates beyond the ten grounds in the eleventh, twelfth and (twelve-and-a-half) thirteenth ground of Vajradhara, where one becomes omniscient.

relations.note: the sūtra system counts ten grounds plus buddhahood

name: Recognising signs, deviations and obstacles as the path

definitions.definition: Knowing that attainments arise in oneself removes hope for them; knowing māras and deviations as one's own path and dependent arising turns faults into qualities (Vajra Verses).

relations.note: the tantric counterpart of lojong's taking adversity as the path

name: The four authorities (tshad ma bzhi) of the Lamdre

definitions.definition: Scripture, the teacher, personal experience and the historical account of the lineage — by which the result of the path is established.

name: The four attachments to be parted from

definitions.definition: Attachment to this life, to saṃsāra, to one's own purpose, and grasping — whose absence is dharma practice, renunciation, bodhicitta and the view.

name: The three principal aspects of the path

definitions.definition: Renunciation, bodhicitta and the correct view: without renunciation one cannot stop pursuing saṃsāra; renunciation without bodhicitta does not lead to buddhahood; neither without the view cuts the root of existence.

relations.note: the Sakya four lines name the same three plus dharma practice

name: The four thoughts that turn the mind (blo ldog rnam bzhi)

definitions.definition: The preliminaries of mind training (Seven Points 1.1): the precious human life, death and impermanence, karma, and the faults of saṃsāra.
The topics of the small and middling scopes that turn the mind from this life and from future lives.
The topics of the impure vision.

name: The Gelug monastic curriculum of the five great texts

definitions.definition: After the Collected Topics, Types of Mind and Types of Reasons, monks debate for many years on five subjects: the Perfection of Wisdom (Abhisamayālaṅkāra), Madhyamaka (Madhyamakāvatāra), Pramāṇa (Pramāṇavārttika), Abhidharma (Abhidharmakośa) and Vinaya (Guṇaprabha's Vinayasūtra), using their college's textbooks; the course ends in the geshe examinations.

notes: Sources: src:bsdus-grwa, src:lorig, src:tarig, src:gelug-yigcha, src:abhisamayalamkara, src:madhyamakavatara, src:pramanavarttika, src:abhidharmakosa, src:vinayasutra-gunaprabha.

name: The method of monastic debate (rtsod pa)

definitions.definition: A standing challenger, opening with Mañjuśrī's syllable 'dhīḥ', poses consequences to a seated defender, clapping and stamping at each point; the defender may answer only 'I accept', 'the reason is not established', 'there is no pervasion' or ask 'why?'; debate is a meditation that sharpens analysis and cuts wrong views.

relations.note: a Tibetan form of Buddhist debate practice

notes: Recalled; symbolism of the clap varies in explanation.

name: The four tenet systems (grub mtha' bzhi)

definitions.definition: Vaibhāṣika, Sautrāntika, Cittamātra and Madhyamaka (Svātantrika, Prāsaṅgika), studied as a ladder of increasingly subtle views, each refuting the grosser object of negation of the one below.

notes: Contribution to the U41 concept; sources: src:precious-garland-of-tenets, src:drubta-chenmo.

name: The object of negation (dgag bya)

definitions.definition: What reasoning must refute is inherent existence — existence from the object's own side, not posited by conceptual designation; to negate less leaves the root of saṃsāra, to negate more destroys conventional existence and falls into nihilism.
Gorampa: in ultimate analysis the four extremes themselves are negated, without Tsongkhapa's qualifier; conventional appearances are not established even conventionally under analysis.

relations.note: Gelug and Sakya differ on whether the negandum is qualified

name: Freedom from elaborations (spros bral)

definitions.definition: The ultimate beyond the four extremes; clinging to emptiness as a negation is itself an extreme (Gorampa).
Accepted in the sense that the meditative wisdom realising emptiness is free of dualistic appearance and of the elaborations of inherent existence.

relations.note: as the MMK's pacification of elaborations

name: The view as the absence of grasping

definitions.definition: 'If grasping arises, it is not the view': the correct view is not a position held but freedom from grasping at any extreme.

name: The inseparability of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa ('khor 'das dbyer med)

definitions.definition: The Sakya view of the Lamdre: the causal continuum, the all-base as union of clarity and emptiness, holds saṃsāra and nirvāṇa inseparably; when obscured it appears as saṃsāra, when purified as nirvāṇa.

name: Tsongkhapa's eight difficult points of Prāsaṅgika

definitions.definition: No ālaya distinct from the six consciousnesses; no reflexive awareness; no autonomous syllogisms; external objects accepted conventionally; śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas realise the selflessness of phenomena; grasping at the self of phenomena is an affliction; disintegration is a functioning thing; hence a unique account of the three times.

name: The four essential points for analysing selflessness

definitions.definition: Identifying the self to be negated; ascertaining that such a self must be either one with or different from the aggregates; ascertaining that it is not one; ascertaining that it is not different.

relations.note: a condensed form of the chariot reasoning

name: The self as mere dependent designation

definitions.definition: The 'mere I' designated in dependence on the aggregates is the conventionally existent self that acts and experiences; the inherently existent self apprehended by innate self-grasping does not exist.

name: The two truths

definitions.definition: All the Buddha's teaching rests on the two truths; conventional truth is false or correct, the ultimate one only; conventional truth is the method, the ultimate what arises from the method.
Two natures of each phenomenon, one found by conventional and the other by ultimate valid cognition; mutually compatible, understood together when the analysis of the view is complete.
For Gorampa the ultimate is beyond mind; the conventional is what appears to mind still affected by ignorance.

name: Mind as clarity and knowing (gsal zhing rig pa)

definitions.definition: The definition of mind in the Types of Mind literature and the object of Gelug Mahāmudrā: mere clarity and knowing, formless, in which objects appear; its ultimate nature is emptiness.
The clarity aspect of the causal continuum's union of clarity and emptiness.

name: The seven types of awareness (blo rig bdun)

definitions.definition: Direct valid cognition, inferential cognition, subsequent cognition, correctly assuming consciousness, awareness to which an object appears without being ascertained, doubt, and wrong consciousness — the classification of the Types of Mind textbooks.

members: snang la ma nges pa (non-ascertaining appearance)
notes: From src:lorig (genre); not tied to a single text here.

name: Gross, subtle and very subtle body and mind

definitions.definition: In Highest Yoga Tantra as Tsongkhapa's tradition explains it: the gross level (sense consciousnesses and the body of flesh), the subtle (conceptual minds and the winds and channels), and the very subtle (the clear-light mind and its wind), which manifests in death, deep sleep and completion-stage practice and continues into buddhahood.

name: Signs of the dissolution of the elements

definitions.definition: In the Vajra Verses, when elements gather in meditation: earth into water — mirage; water into fire — smoke; fire into wind — fireflies; wind into consciousness — a burning lamp; consciousness into clear light — like a cloudless sky.

The eight stages of dying in the Guhyasamāja-based Gelug presentation: mirage, smoke, fireflies, flickering flame, then the white appearance, red increase, black near-attainment and the clear light of death — also re-enacted in completion-stage practice.

name: The perfection vehicle and the mantra vehicle

definitions.definition: Awakening is accomplished relying on both secret mantra and the perfections; Atiśa's conduct texts explain only the perfection side.
The two Mahāyāna vehicles share the same view of emptiness; mantra is superior through deity yoga, the union of method and wisdom in one consciousness, and so is faster.

name: Deity yoga

definitions.definition: The feature distinguishing mantra from the perfection vehicle: the wisdom realising emptiness itself appears as the deity's body.

name: Gelug Mahāmudrā (the Ganden oral lineage)

definitions.definition: Mahāmudrā in the sūtra approach (emptiness of the mind as Nāgārjuna taught) and the mantra approach (clear light of great bliss); meditation first on the conventional nature of mind, then on its emptiness; the various Mahāmudrā and Dzogchen instructions are said to converge in one intent.

name: Exchanging self and other

definitions.definition: The heart of mind training: reversing the objects of self-cherishing and other-cherishing, enacted by sending and taking (Seven Points 2.6; Eight Verses 7).
The second of the two methods of generating bodhicitta, from Śāntideva; the Guru Pūjā makes it the heart of practice.
Taught as the 'practice of a bodhisattva' by Tokmé Zangpo.

name: Equalizing self and other

definitions.definition: The first part of the Śāntideva method: since all equally wish happiness and not suffering, there is no reason to cherish oneself more.

name: The sevenfold cause-and-effect instruction for bodhicitta

definitions.definition: On the basis of equanimity: recognising all beings as mothers, remembering their kindness, wishing to repay it, love, compassion, the extraordinary resolve, and bodhicitta — the first six being causes, the seventh the effect; traced to Atiśa's lineage.

name: The kindness of all beings

definitions.definition: All beings are to be held dear and their kindness contemplated — as mothers in past lives and as the field in which one gains merit and patience.

name: Taking adversity as the path

definitions.definition: When the world is full of wrongdoing, adverse conditions are transformed into the path by blaming self-cherishing, contemplating others' kindness, seeing appearances as the four bodies, and the four practices.
Taking on others' wrongdoing when harmed without cause (Thirty-Seven Practices 13).

name: The five powers of mind training

definitions.definition: The whole practice condensed for a lifetime and for the time of death: resolve, familiarisation, the white seed, repudiation (of self-cherishing) and aspiration.

name: The commitments of mind training

definitions.definition: The sixth point: sixteen (in the later arrangement) rules — abiding by the three general points, not speaking of others' faults, abandoning hope of results, not letting the practice become pride, and so on.

name: The precepts of mind training

definitions.definition: The seventh point: twenty-one (in the later arrangement) guidelines — doing everything with one intention, resolving at the start and reviewing at the end of the day, meditating on those who provoke one, training impartially and wholeheartedly.

name: Ultimate bodhicitta in mind training

definitions.definition: Regarding all phenomena as dreams, examining the unborn nature of awareness, letting even the remedy be released in its own place, resting in the nature of the all-base, and being an illusory being between sessions.

name: Relative bodhicitta in mind training

definitions.definition: Sending and taking mounted on the breath, beginning with oneself, applied to the three objects and poisons, and supported by slogans in all activities.

name: Adversity as the return of one's own deeds

definitions.definition: Whatever harm befalls one is the wheel of one's own past deeds returning; the fitting response is to turn the weapon on self-grasping.

name: Renunciation (definite emergence)

definitions.definition: The first principal aspect: the wish for liberation arising day and night, from contemplating the leisure and endowment, death, karma and the sufferings of saṃsāra.
Not being attached to saṃsāra.

name: Bodhicitta

definitions.definition: Generated after refuge and love on seeing beings' suffering; the aspiring mind must be held by the engaging vow.
The only door to the Mahāyāna.

name: Aspiring and engaging bodhicitta

definitions.definition: Aspiring bodhicitta does not grow without the vow of the engaging mind, which requires prātimokṣa as its basis.

name: Analytical and placement meditation

definitions.definition: Two modes of meditation, both necessary: analytical (dpyad sgom) investigates with discernment and is required for faith, renunciation, bodhicitta and emptiness; placement ('jog sgom) holds the mind one-pointedly; in insight analysis itself induces pliancy.

relations.note: Tsongkhapa rejects the claim that all analysis obstructs meditation

name: The union of calm abiding and insight

definitions.definition: Calm abiding brings the superknowledges, but only the yoga of the perfection of wisdom joined with method exhausts the obscurations.
Achieved when analysis of emptiness itself induces pliancy and stability; like a bright, unflickering lamp.

name: The nine stages of calm abiding

definitions.definition: Placing, continuous placing, repeated placing, close placing, taming, pacifying, thorough pacifying, one-pointedness and equipoise; achieved through six powers and four attentions, with the five faults and eight antidotes, following the Śrāvakabhūmi and Madhyāntavibhāga.

name: The six powers for calm abiding

definitions.definition: Hearing (1st state), reflection (2nd), mindfulness (3rd–4th), introspective alertness (5th–6th), effort (7th–8th) and complete familiarity (9th).

name: The four attentions (mental engagements)

definitions.definition: Tight focus (1st–2nd states), interrupted engagement (3rd–7th), uninterrupted engagement (8th) and spontaneous engagement (9th).

name: The prerequisites (limbs) of calm abiding

definitions.definition: Abiding in the limbs of calm taught in the Samādhisambhāraparivarta, without which no concentration is achieved even in thousands of years.
A suitable place, few desires, contentment, few activities, pure ethics, abandoning conceptual thoughts of desire and the like.

name: Pliancy as the measure of calm abiding

definitions.definition: After the ninth state, mental pliancy arises, then physical pliancy with its bliss; when that joy settles, calm abiding is achieved; before it there is only a likeness of calm abiding.

name: The superknowledges as necessary for benefiting beings

definitions.definition: Like a bird without grown wings, one without superknowledges cannot work for beings; they depend on calm abiding and should be sought with effort for the sake of others.

name: Mindfulness of death: three roots, nine reasons, three decisions

definitions.definition: Death is certain, its time uncertain, and at death only dharma helps — each with three reasons — leading to the resolves to practise, to practise now, and to practise purely.

name: The four general characteristics of karma

definitions.definition: Karma is definite, grows greatly, is not met if not done, and once done is not lost.

name: The four opponent powers

definitions.definition: Purification of wrongdoing by the power of repudiation (regret), of reliance (refuge and bodhicitta), of the remedy (virtuous practice) and of restraint (resolving not to repeat).

name: The three kinds of suffering (Buddhist)

definitions.definition: The suffering of suffering (manifest pain), the suffering of change (pleasure that turns to pain) and pervasive conditioned suffering (the appropriated aggregates themselves).

relations.note: Sāṃkhya's threefold suffering (internal, external, divine) is a different classification

name: The realms of rebirth

definitions.definition: The hells, hungry ghosts and animals (lower realms) contemplated by the small scope; gods, demigods and humans (higher realms) whose sufferings are contemplated by the middling scope.

name: The precious human life of leisure and endowment

definitions.definition: A human life free of the eight unfree states and having the ten endowments, of great value and hard to find by cause, example and number.

name: Going for refuge to the Three Jewels

definitions.definition: Taken three times, kneeling with joined palms, after offerings and the seven-limb worship; the entrance to all practice.
Arises from fear and faith; one knows the qualities of the Three Jewels and keeps the precepts of refuge.

name: The three trainings

definitions.definition: Training well in ethics, concentration and wisdom while abiding in the engaging vow, with purified body, speech and mind.
The path to liberation of the middling scope, with ethics as its foundation.

name: The three vows (sdom gsum)

definitions.definition: The prātimokṣa vow is the basis of the bodhisattva vow; celibates may not take the secret and wisdom empowerments.
Prātimokṣa, bodhisattva and mantra vows are each to be kept by their own rules and not mixed (Sakya Paṇḍita).
A monk holds all three; the tantric vows and pledges are guarded as one's life.

name: The root downfalls of the bodhisattva vow

definitions.definition: The eighteen root downfalls (from the Ākāśagarbha-sūtra as compiled by Śāntideva) and forty-six secondary faults (after Asaṅga), taught in Tsongkhapa's commentary on the ethics chapter of the Bodhisattvabhūmi.

notes: Counts recalled; the source commentary (byang chub gzhung lam) is not entered as a source here.

name: The fourteen root downfalls of the tantric vow

definitions.definition: The fourteen root downfalls (beginning with disparaging the vajra master) whose avoidance is the core of the tantric vow, as explained in Tsongkhapa's 'Fruit Clusters of Siddhis'.
Sakya Paṇḍita's Three Vows treats the tantric vow's rules as distinct from the lower vows.

notes: Title of Tsongkhapa's commentary recalled with low confidence.

name: The seven noble riches

definitions.definition: Faith, ethics, shame, conscience (consideration), learning, generosity and wisdom — seven inexhaustible treasures to adorn oneself with instead of material things.

notes: In the Tibetan of Jewel Garland v7–8 'khrel yod ngo tsha shes pa' is one 'wealth'; the seven are counted with learning, giving and wisdom.

name: Liberation and omniscience in the Gelug

definitions.definition: Liberation (nirvāṇa) is the final cessation of the afflictive obscurations by the wisdom directly realising emptiness; buddhahood (omniscience) is the further removal of the obscurations to knowledge, which only bodhicitta-motivated practice accomplishes.
The obscurations of afflictions and of knowables are exhausted only by the perfection of wisdom joined with method.

name: Proper reliance on the spiritual teacher

definitions.definition: The root of the path: relying in thought (faith seeing the teacher as a buddha, respect remembering kindness) and in deed (offering, service and practice); the teacher must have the ten qualities.
The spiritual friend through whom faults are exhausted is to be cherished more than one's body.

name: The qualified teacher

definitions.definition: For the bodhisattva vow, one skilled in its rite, abiding in it, patient and compassionate (Lamp 23–24); for mantra, a master able to give the complete empowerment.
The ten qualities of the Mahāyāna teacher (disciplined, serene, pacified, superior in qualities, energetic, learned, realised in reality, skilled in speech, loving, tireless).

name: The four greatnesses of the lamrim teaching

definitions.definition: Understanding all teachings as non-contradictory; taking all scriptures as instructions; easily finding the Conqueror's intent; being saved from the great misdeed of rejecting the dharma.

name: The seven divine dharmas of the Kadam

definitions.definition: The four deities — Śākyamuni, Avalokiteśvara, Tārā, Acala — and the three baskets.

name: The six Kadam treatises (bka' gdams gzhung drug)

definitions.definition: Bodhisattvabhūmi, Mahāyānasūtrālaṅkāra, Śikṣāsamuccaya, Bodhicaryāvatāra, Jātakamālā and Udānavarga — the texts studied in Potowa's textual tradition.

name: The transmission and secrecy of the Lamdre

definitions.definition: The long lineage runs Virūpa — Kāṇha — Ḍamarupa — Avadhūtipa — Gayadhara — Drokmi — (Seton Kunrig — Zhangtön Chöbar) — Sachen; the short lineage from Virūpa directly to Sachen in vision. The Vajra Verses were long kept unwritten; Sachen was told to keep the teaching secret for years; the Lobshé remained a restricted explanation for close disciples.

notes: Lineage order and the secrecy period recalled; check against Sakya histories.

name: Succession by recognised reincarnation (Dalai and Panchen Lamas)

definitions.definition: Leading lamas are recognised as the rebirths of their predecessors: the Dalai Lamas as emanations of Avalokiteśvara, the Panchen Lamas of Amitābha; the title 'Dalai' dates from Altan Khan's gift to Sönam Gyatso (1578), applied back to his two predecessors.

name: The three activities of the learned

definitions.definition: Composition, exposition and debate, each governed by its rules (Sakya Paṇḍita's Gateway to Learning).

name: Cosmology in the Gelug curriculum

definitions.definition: The Abhidharmakośa's world system (Mount Meru, four continents, the desire, form and formless realms, the eon cycle) studied as the conventional cosmology, alongside the Kālacakra's different system; both are taught as conventional presentations.

name: The union of method and wisdom

definitions.definition: Wisdom without method and method without wisdom are both bondage; method is all the perfections other than wisdom.
